name: Idiopathic Recurrent Pericarditis

criteria.description: Recurrent episodes of sharp, pleuritic chest pain typical of pericarditis
Pericardial friction rub detected on auscultation during acute episodes
Electrocardiogram showing widespread ST elevation or PR depression during episodes
Evidence of pericardial effusion on echocardiography or imaging
Elevated C-reactive protein (CRP) or erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) during episodes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: At least two major criteria including recurrent pericardial chest pain plus either pericardial friction rub, ECG changes, or pericardial effusion, supported by elevated inflammatory markers
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of secondary causes such as infection, autoimmune disease, or malignancy

pathognomonic.symptomName: Sharp pleuritic chest pain worsened by inspiration and lying supine

rare.symptomName: Autoimmune manifestations such as rash or arthritis

laboratory: Normal cardiac enzymes (troponin usually normal or mildly elevated)
imaging: Electrocardiogram with diffuse ST-segment elevation and PR depression
Chest X-ray may show enlarged cardiac silhouette if effusion is large
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; idiopathic etiology
other: Pericardial fluid analysis typically sterile and inflammatory
Exclusion of infectious, autoimmune, and neoplastic causes is essential

distinguishingFeatures: Positive microbial cultures or PCR from pericardial fluid
Systemic signs of infection such as high fever and leukocytosis
Presence of systemic autoimmune disease markers (ANA, RF)
Other organ involvement such as arthritis, rash, or renal disease
Detection of malignant cells in pericardial fluid
History of known malignancy or suspicious imaging findings

redFlags: Signs of cardiac tamponade (hypotension, jugular venous distension, muffled heart sounds)
Persistent high fever unresponsive to NSAIDs
Progressive constrictive pericarditis with heart failure symptoms
references: Imazio M, et al. Recurrent pericarditis: new and emerging therapeutic options. Nat Rev Cardiol. 2017.
